chunks: From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

Al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays and I bought food in al-Madīnah, and evening came upon us before we could move it. So we left it in the market in its sacks and departed. When the next morning came, we went early to the market, and there were the people of the market gathered around a black man whom they had seized, and he had stolen a sack of our food. They said to us, "This man has stolen a sack from your food, so bring him to the governor." We disliked to proceed with that until we knew the view of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Then al-Muʿallā entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and mentioned that to him, so he ordered us to bring him forward. So we brought him forward, and his hand was cut off.

key_terms.جُوَالِيقِهِ: its sacks or bag-containers in which the food was stored
key_terms.رَأْيَ: the judgment or legal view sought from the Imam
key_terms.فَقُطِعَ: his hand was cut off as the legal punishment
key_terms.ٱلسُّوقِ: the marketplace where the goods were left and the theft was discovered
key_terms.ٱلْوَالِي: the governing authority to whom the accused was to be referred

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the process of referring a theft case to the authority for the hadd punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a case of theft in al-Madīnah in which the complainants refrained from taking legal action until they learned the judgment of Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. It reflects the implementation of the hadd punishment for theft through referral to the governing authority and shows deference to the Imam’s legal guidance.
